summary: Temporary trade pauses and falling crude oil prices defined the week, providing immediate cost relief and stabilizing freight surcharges for both Indian and Chinese logistics operators. While China's extended tariff and port fee waivers preserve short-term transpacific shipping stability, India is aggressively positioning for long-term supply chain realignment through massive maritime infrastructure investments and an impending US trade deal. Moving forward, these dynamics suggest short-term freight cost predictability will soon give way to a structural shift in global trade lanes, with South Asian ports capturing a larger share of ocean container traffic away from traditional China-centric routes.
